findings.title: The UNMAPPED_SIGNAL_CAP bound is not enforced, and four changed documents claim it is
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutant: write.ts:604 `for (const code of fresh)` -> `for (const code of fresh.slice(0, UNMAPPED_SIGNAL_CAP - signalledUnmappedCodes.size))` — the correctly-bounded form. Survived 29/29. NOT equivalent: under the mutant a code that WAS named in the capture is left unmarked and is re-reported by a later call, breaking the stated "IT REPORTS EACH DISTINCT CODE ONCE" contract; under HEAD the Set instead grows past the cap. The two differ observably and no case can tell them apart, because every cap-adjacent case feeds exactly one code per call. NOT on an unexecuted branch: write.ts:604 runs in most cases in the describe block. Static half of the proof: write.ts:571 tests `size` BEFORE :604 adds every element of `fresh`, and `rg signalledUnmappedCodes` finds exactly one growth site (604) and no trim site (359 decl, 411 clear, 568 has, 571 size, 604 add) — so with size==0 and a 20-code call, `0 >= 8` is false and the Set reaches 20. Worst case is UNMAPPED_SIGNAL_CAP-1+fresh.length for an input the signature types as readonly string[] and the docblock calls unbounded. Falsified: write.ts:353-354 ("holds at most UNMAPPED_SIGNAL_CAP distinct codes and then stops growing"), docs/directory.md:905 ("BOUNDED at UNMAPPED_SIGNAL_CAP distinct codes"), .claude/reference/arch-review-log.md:1663 ("Now a bounded per-code Set"), deviations D10 line 217 ("Now a bounded Set").

findings.title: Runbook claim "the only one above warning" is false — withLedgerAttribution and the new overflow marker are both error-level subsystem:refusal_ledger emitters
findings.reason: worker/jobs/response-generation/persist.ts:1048-1052 is Sentry.captureException(error, { level: 'error', tags: { subsystem: 'refusal_ledger', ... } }) and has been since #1079; src/lib/refusals/write.ts:639-642, added in this same diff, is a second error-level emitter under the same tag. At HEAD four emitters carry subsystem:refusal_ledger — one warning (write.ts:479-484) and three error. An operator building the rule this row asks for would reach for `subsystem:refusal_ledger AND level:error` and also catch every ledger-write exception plus the overflow marker. The companion "a FOURTH caller" half is not independently falsifiable: line 55 sets a local convention of counting only warnLedgerDisabled's callers.

findings.title: The overflow marker's durable log transport has no oracle anywhere in the codebase
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutant: the entire logger.warn block deleted from noteUnmappedOverflow. Survived 29/29 of write.test.ts, which the reverse-import sweep proves is the ONLY suite reaching this function (importers of noteUnmappedBlockReasons/UNMAPPED_*/noteUnmappedOverflow are write.ts, write.test.ts, persist.ts, persist.test.ts and docs). EXECUTED: the cap case's ['one_too_many'] call enters noteUnmappedOverflow and runs the block; the case simply asserts nothing about it. NOT equivalent: it removes a transport. Load-bearing by the module's own doctrine — write.ts:601-603 and docs/directory.md:905 both state the latch is set when captureMessage RETURNS (queued, not delivered) and that "the log line above is what makes that acceptable"; noteUnmappedOverflow latches unmappedOverflowSignalled on the same queued-return terms at write.ts:644. With the capture queued-but-undelivered and the log line gone, the fact that more than eight codes escaped the union exists nowhere for the life of the process, with no retry. Fix is one assertion in the cap case.

findings.title: noteUnmappedOverflow's Sentry catch — the "shares the SAME cooldown" claim — is on a branch no case executes

findings.reason: §1a-do (line 243) is "every unconfigured rule, in one sitting": a six-row table of # | Rule name | _If_ filter | _When_ trigger | Level, closed by "_Then_ action for all six" at line 358. Neither fault:unmapped_block_reason nor fault:unmapped_block_reason_overflow gets a row, so an operator who works §1a-do end to end builds six rules and catches neither signal; no cadence is stated anywhere, and for a constant-message error "first seen" versus a frequency is exactly the decision the runbook itself argues at lines 361-365. Precedent, not excuse: the #1009 sibling item has the same missing row and is one of the two line 353 records.

Four interpolate bounded values (circuit-breaker.ts:197, subscription-updated.ts:154, OnboardingDemoWorker.ts:148, write.ts:479 whose only interpolation is a compile-time constant). generate-draft.ts:77 interpolates businessId, opening one Sentry issue group per business, and §1a-do rule 2 (cost_event:limit_exceeded) fires on "issue is first seen", so the fragmentation multiplies pages.
